messages.text: The library has that San Fernando Cemetery map you asked about. I can set it aside with the local history handouts.
Thank you. I am putting those loose certificates in one folder before Thursday so I do not arrive with a paper avalanche.
Good. Also, if the two-night plan south is shifting, those maps will keep until April.
That is where it landed. The hotel can wait after the tire and dental bill.
Coffee tomorrow still good? I may bring that menu tree from my neighbor's repair shop. It keeps sending billing calls to parts.
Still good. Have him print the extension list and the after-hours greeting. Usually the bad branch is one digit buried under another digit.
You make it sound like untangling cords behind the old board, except now the cords are invisible.
Same habit, different box. Map the route, write the plain words, then test it from outside.
Wednesday coffee at the Hyde Park spot? 9:30 work for you, or are you stuck on a call?
9:30 is fine. Only got one short call this week, Tuesday afternoon. Wednesdays are wide open again.
Right, the new schedule. Still weird seeing you free midweek.
Getting used to it. Bringing the sketchbook this time, finally have a morning to sit with it.

Pulled the shortlist for the March 26 talk. Right now it's Reuben Diaz (printmaker, east side), Mei Ann Wong (textile, just back from Marfa residency), and Jorge Saldaña (sound work at the Mexic-Arte). Thoughts?
Good lineup. Last three months we've leaned heavy on painters and most of them looked like me on the flyer. Let's confirm Mei Ann and Jorge first, see if Reuben can do April.
Agreed. I'll send Mei Ann the ask tonight. Also: the Blanton has that Latinx Diaspora panel Thursday at 6:30, want to scout it together? Could pull a guest from there too.
Yes. I'll meet you at the front entrance 6:15.
Can you look at the flyer draft tonight and tell me if the chairs/mic note is missing?
Yes, after supper. Tomorrow morning is Miguel at Quack's, so I'll send edits before I leave.
Perfect. Keep it to the practical fixes; I can add the warmer wording.
That works. I like seeing everyone there, but one clean note is better than a dozen texts.
Dad, Mateo's robotics pickup moved to 5:30 Friday. Can you cover if I get stuck at the office?
I can do 5:30. I had dinner penciled in with Sandra at 7, but I will keep it on this side of town.
Thank you. And do not let my schedule make you cancel every pleasant thing you put on your calendar.
It is just enchiladas and conversation. I will get Mateo first and text Sandra if traffic is bad.
Sunday still work for Round Rock? Lucas has robotics until 11:15, so noon is easier.
Noon works. I can bring the enchiladas if you want to skip the restaurant crowd.
Bring them. Mom may send the insurance copy with me, just FYI.
That's fine. I'll look it over and send it back the same way.
Found it finally. William and Sarah's marriage record from 1892 - Sevier County, Tennessee. His parents came over from Cornwall in 1854, not Devon like Dad always said.
Cornwall, huh. Dad would argue with you from beyond the grave.

The census matches the clerk's spelling, so I'm going with it. Putting copies in the binder for Sunday lunch. Also - Smithville Chapel still has the family page in their old record book. I asked Pastor Lyle if they'll scan it.
Good. I should drive up there myself one of these years. Been telling myself that since Mama's funeral and that was 2009.
For Saturday, I am voting Lady Bird Lake. The Hill Country option has too much loose rock on the way back down.
Lady Bird works. I will bring the poles anyway and skip trying to prove anything on the slopes.
Good. Also wear the newer shoes, not the old brown pair you wore near Enchanted Rock.
Already by the door. I put two Advil in the side pocket just in case, but I probably will not need them.
Hyde Park at 10 still good? Their drip went up again, because apparently coffee needed a city council hearing.
Still good. I penciled in $8 for it after Sunday, so I am skipping the muffin.
That old Honda taking you there, or is it in the shop again?
It is fine. Just gas and the inspection sticker this month. The title folder is still in the glove box where it belongs.
Coffee still good for 10? I also found that clip on replacing the Delta cartridge without tearing up the tile.
Council agenda for next Tuesday is up. Item 14 is the bond package for the East Riverside transit corridor and Item 22 is the homeless services contract renewal.
10 works. Send it over. I may try it Sunday with the pregame on low in the kitchen.
Saw it. I'll show up for both. Transit piece is overdue, but I want to read the bond numbers carefully before I cheer. Dad used to say never sign anything you haven't run twice.
Sent. If the bullpen gives up another late one, maybe aim the wrench away from anything breakable.
Good advice. I will keep the radio and the tools on opposite sides of the counter.
Ha. Your dad and mine would have gotten along. You going to email Pool's office again about the water rates?
Yeah, drafting it tonight. Rates plus the rezoning near Springdale. If we lose another block of those duplexes, working folks won't have anywhere left to land.
The back room at Cherrywood has a three-piece Thursday. Upright bass, brushes, no amplifiers trying to win a war.
If the door stays at $12, I could do that after dinner.
Listed as $12 cash, 7:30. Maybe forty chairs if they squeeze them.
That size is about right. Half an hour in a place like that usually straightens out the day.
Wednesday coffee still good? The place on Duval has that back patio, though the air gets rough when the evening crowd starts.
Coffee is good. Let's take the inside corner table. If I bring anything for the Rangers opener later, it'll be one Pearl Snap and one Modelo, nothing fancy.
That tracks. I will leave the tall cans to the younger knees and worse judgment.
Mine can stay in the fridge until the weekend. Two is plenty for a game.
For Saturday setup, can you still do the chairs? The gallery floor is slick near the back door.
I can. I am wearing the old Merrells one more month, so I will move slowly on that floor.
Slow is fine. Did that bill from Dr. Lenz finally settle?
Settled, yes. I put $110 toward the Visa this morning and left the shoe replacement for April.
For tomorrow's setup, can you bring that green bowl again? It disappeared fast last month.
I can. I'll make it after I trim the cilantro pot. The basil still looks sad, so don't count on that.
Perfect. Maybe put the peppery one beside the chips and a gentler one near the sign-in table.
Fair. I still have not lived down the January batch.
Found another folder from the old house on Bouldin. Mom kept your second grade report card and a clipping from the Statesman about the South Austin Little League season.
I finally pulled the folder from the genealogy meeting. Dad's old employment card from Stuckey Auto Supply is in there, with the manager line and the 1971 date.
From the Bouldin place? I thought everything went in the boxes when we moved to the Travis Heights side.
Oh good. He kept everything from that counter, even the parts catalogs. I still remember him quizzing me on part numbers at the kitchen table.
Most of it did. This was in the cedar chest. There's a photo of the four of us on the porch the summer before I started high school, so 1972 I think. You had that awful haircut.
Scan it and send. I want to see Dad in those glasses again. Bring the folder Sunday and I'll sort with you.
Mom's stuff is thinner. Just her diploma and the certificate from the secretarial program at Durham Business School. I'll scan both and send you the PDF.
Send the scans whenever. I want to print one for Emily so the grandson has something for that family tree assignment.
Found another folder in the hall closet today. Mom kept your acceptance letter from UT-Austin, the one for the fall after high school. Did you want it for your records?
Wow. Hold onto it for me. That feels like a long time ago.
I will. There's also a photo of you on the Drag from sophomore year. Funny to think that's the last campus picture before you started on the switchboards.
Bring it to lunch next time. I'll laugh at the haircut.
Saturday I might be 10 minutes late. I want to drop my ballot in the Randalls box on Brodie first.
No rush. I mailed mine Tuesday after I went through the booklet from Howson.
Did the booklet have the ACC trustee race? I had no idea who two of those people were.
Yes, all four candidates, with their answers side by side. That race is why I won't skip the down-ballot stuff.
Saw a reel from that ceramicist in East Austin — she just announced a small show at Wally Workman. Tagging you so it shows up in your saved.
Got it, saved. She is the one whose studio Blanton featured last year, right?
Yes. Also can you re-share our March talk flyer on Facebook? Your neighborhood group always gets the most clicks. I never get traction over there.
Will post it to the Hyde Park page tonight and tag a couple of the old museum docent folks. That side moves better for me.
How are things holding up this month, Ty? You sounded a little wrung out on the phone Sunday.
Better now. Wagner check finally cleared yesterday — $1,450 for February. Leaner than I'd like, but it's something.
Was that a slow stretch for them, or for you?
Them mostly. A couple of their projects paused so some weeks I was only at 14 hours. March is looking back to normal already.
Did the Cedar Bend item clear yet? You sounded irritated with the new portal last night.
Cleared this morning. $1,650, same as I wrote in the notebook. I moved it myself before lunch.
Good. Do the next practical thing, then. What does your March sheet show now?
With groceries, prescriptions, truck gas, and the utilities already entered, it shows $2,214 so far. I will keep the rest quiet.
The lake path is dry. Do you want the flatter loop before the heat settles in?
Yes. Just the loop and coffee after if my knee is decent. I have art setup emails waiting at home.
I'll tell the others 7:15 at the Lamar footbridge. Bring poles, not pride.
Thanks. I saw Miguel Wednesday, so he already gave me enough commentary for one week.
Can you do Lady Bird at 7:30 next Saturday, or is the 31st Street maintenance slot still on your calendar?
They moved it to Tuesday morning. Same little place, same sticky bedroom window.
After five Austin summers, that window has earned a formal complaint.
I wrote it down with the lease packet so I don't forget.
Weather app says Saturday is kinder before 8. Lady Bird Lake, starting at the Pfluger bridge?
That works. If we step off at 6:50, I can get the quiet stretch near the water before bikes take over.
I will bring the route map. Knee-friendly pace, no heroics.
Good. I will bring water and leave the heavier shoes by the door tonight.
Can you bring the blue folder Sunday? I can look at the new premium sheet after lunch.
Yes. I also wrote the pharmacy totals on the front page so we can compare them with January.
Good. Keep the receipt from Walgreens too. Sometimes the card order changes at the counter.
I put it with the cuff notebook and the lab slip so everything is in one place.
I am glad you called earlier. Did you get the folder sorted, or did the whole pile go back on the chair?
Half sorted. I wrote the rest in the paper book for Tuesday. The kitchen is clean, and that helped more than staring at it.
Good. Do the next practical thing, then leave the rest alone tonight.
That is the plan. Tea, two chapters, lights out before the late news gets me wound up.
If your arm is still sore, we can keep Saturday to the flat loop by the boardwalk.
It is only a little tender. Dr. Patel said walking is fine, just no hero pace.
Good. I checked the county page too, and the March clinic hours matched what you told me.
That is why I like checking the plain notice instead of the forwarded screenshots.
Saw the photo Emily sent from Saturday. Looked like a sturdy crowd, all ages. Were the folks running it organized?
Pretty organized. Speakers stuck to the time, water out front, table on the side for the bail and legal aid fund. I put $40 in on the way out.
That sounds like a reasonable thing to do. Mama would've put in five and called it good. Did anybody from the family hear about it?
I told Emily Sunday at lunch. She had questions. Good ones. We sat with it for a while.
Saturday route question: Lady Bird again, or the flatter Hill Country loop? Your call on the knee.
Lady Bird is fine. I'd rather keep showing up than baby it and skip. Poles in the car already.
That's the Tyler answer. 6:55 at the cottonwood?
6:55. If I said it, I'll be there.
The Blanton email has a Mexico City mural lecture on March 26. Thought of you immediately.
Put it on my list. I skipped the frame sale today and sent that $24 to the folder instead.
That is very you. If you ever get there, I expect photos of walls, not restaurant plates.
Walls first. Cheap lunch second.

Tyler, Marlene from church forwarded me this article saying the new shingles vaccine is part of a tracking program. She is very worked up about it. Before I say anything back to her, can you look at where it came from?
Send me the link. Do not forward it on yet.
Here. healthtruthdaily-dot-net. The byline is just 'Staff.'

Domain was registered last August, no editor listed, the photo is lifted from a 2019 Reuters piece. It is the same kind of thing the Tuesday folks keep bringing me from their text messages. Tell Marlene to check the CDC page directly, and I can walk her through it next week if she wants. I have lost the patience I used to have for this stuff after the last two years.
Are you still doing that 3:30 court thing today? Please do not overdo the quick side steps before your weekend miles.
Yes, just a few easy games. The little side shuffles are the point, not winning.
Good. Karen sent me a photo from Lady Bird last time, and you looked steadier than you sounded.
Saturday helped. If storms stay away, I will be there again with the cap and water bottle.
The print shop says the flyer batch will be $42 if we approve by 5. I can front it if that is easier.
Thanks, but I will pay my half tonight. I would rather settle small things right away.
Very you. I will send the receipt after they run the card.
Good. I already moved the art-talk line around after Sunday, and I do not want it drifting.
Still aiming for 9:30 at Flightpath? I have the Rangers box and that council agenda you asked for.
Yes. I can stay until 10:20. Nora needs the room count before lunch.
Good. I will spare you my full bullpen speech.
Appreciated. Save the old radio-room story for the second cup.
For the April talk - I want to pitch Roland Cabrera. He just wrapped a portrait series on Iraq-era field medics, small show at Camp Mabry's gallery last week.
Don't know him. Through any of your people?
Residency list. I thought you might have a contact over there from your circles, or maybe someone at Tarrytown Chapel who could co-host the conversation piece.
Nope on both counts. Never been past Camp Mabry's gate in my life, and I haven't sat on a chapel committee since the Clinton years. Just reach out to Roland direct. I'll handle chairs and the mic.
I found the Brizendine folder from the Georgetown group. Do you want me to bring it when you come up?
Yes, please. Emily asked about the old Austin addresses, and Lucas liked the photo of Dad's shop.
I will set it by the door. Also, keep Linda's envelope separate if it has Emily's forms mixed in.
Already did. One folder for family records, one for the practical paperwork.
Did you ever find Mama's envelope with the San Antonio addresses?
Yes. It is in the folder I took last week, behind the marriage license copy.
Good. Please do not hurry the courthouse and cemetery stops if this month is already tight.
I agree. I crossed out the March dates and kept the list for later.
You already get your miles in? I saw 84 by lunch. Austin is showing off early.
Just got back from the creek loop. Better when the light is low and nobody is leaf-blowing yet.
Respect. I am still negotiating with my coffee maker.
Coffee tastes better after forty quiet minutes outside.
Coffee still on? I can bring that scanner if you want to digitize the Linda-and-Emily box.
Still on. The box has school photos, old tax copies, and some court-stamped pages from 2006. I should stop letting it live in the closet.
Bring only what you actually want scanned. Wednesday coffee should not become a records warehouse.
Fair. Also no jokes if I ask whether Sandra texted back while we are there.
You see the council item on the wildfire dispatch contract? Renewal vote Thursday.
Saw it. The current vendor's response times slipped twice last summer. I want to see who actually shows up to administer it before I'm impressed.
Same. Three reorgs in five years and nobody owns it.
That's the part that bugs me. People will swing a bond, then nobody bothers to ride the program to make sure it works.
Sending the Cactus Cafe listing. Two guitars and fiddle, seated show, $10 advance. Very Tyler-sized room.
That one sounds better than the big outdoor thing. Ten dollars is easy enough.
Agreed. Doors at 7. You would actually hear the hands on the strings in there.
Put me down as likely. I could use something quiet but not silent.
If the artist ships the small projector to you, can your building desk hold it until setup?
Yes, as long as they put Tyler and unit 204 on the label. The desk knows my box routine by now.
Perfect. I'll keep it small; no giant crate for your hallway.
Good. My hall closet is already losing to folding chairs and the old easel.
Sunday is still good. Mateo voted for the rolled pan if you're up for bringing it.
I can do one pan and a pot of beans. I bought tortillas yesterday.
Great. Please remember he has practice after lunch, so no fire-breathing spoonfuls before the car ride.
I'll keep the sharper bowl for grownups and use the balcony cilantro if it has enough leaves.
Grandson's family tree thing is due Friday. Teacher wants jobs and schools for great-grandparents. Can you fill in your side?
Sure. Both finished at Travis High. Grandpa did a trade course after that and ran the counter at Stuckey Auto Supply on Burnet for almost 30 years.
Perfect, that's what he needs. What about Grandma?
She did Durham Business School after high school, then the front office at Pflugerville Elementary. She knew every kid's name within a week.
Coffee at the Hyde Park place still good? They put us in line on that bare floor last time like it was a city hearing.
Let us grab the table by the window if it is open. Too long standing there and I start walking like an old folding chair.
I will get there early and claim seats. Bring the walking sticks if you are coming from the trail; I will not make jokes until cup two.
Cup two is generous. I used one Advil after last Saturday, so the sticks are coming.
Still on for Wednesday coffee? Hyde Park, usual time?
Yeah, but can we push to 9? Heavier week than I planned — already 24 hours on the Wagner stuff and another deliverable due Friday.
They keeping you busy.
Better than the dry stretch in Feb. SS hit on the 3rd, same $2,300 as always, no raise this year. Consulting has to fill the rest.
For the art talk reception, I ordered sparkling water and tea. Should I add beer, or is that too much for a weeknight crowd?
Maybe one small cooler. If you see Live Oak Pilz or Pacifico, that is more my speed. I will probably just have one while we stack chairs.
Perfect. I will skip the big dark cans the vendor suggested and keep the table near the front doors.
Front doors help. I like leaving with my jacket smelling like a gallery, not the parking lot.
How did your morning numbers look after cutting back on the canned soup?
Better than Tuesday. I wrote them down before breakfast like Dr. Rao asked.
Good. Do the next practical thing. Did the pharmacy give you the lower price this time?
Yes, both generics were under twenty together. I kept the little printout for Emily.
A lady from church sent me that long message about the new spring clinic. It sounded a little breathless.
Send me the link, not the screenshot, and I will compare it with the CDC page and Dr. Patel's office note.
Thank you. I would rather not pass along something that turns out to be nonsense.
Same here. If the clinic hours and age line match, I will put it in my folder.
I found the photo of you at Aunt Ruth's office, sleeves rolled up by that big plug board. Would you like it for the folder?
Yes, please. Funny seeing that next to Monday's notes about cloud handsets and the shared message box.
You always did have patience for getting people to answer in the right order.
The tools changed, but the order still matters. First ring, backup ring, clear wording, written record.
Radar looks clear until 10. Lady Bird is flatter than the Barton Creek option if your knee prefers sensible choices.
Flatter is fine. I had enough sideways work Tuesday to remind me I am not twenty.
Then 7:10 at the Long Center side. I will tell Sam we are skipping the rocky stretch.
I will be there unless the sky changes its mind.
Tomorrow's trail has loose rock after mile two. Please do not bring the smooth-bottom pair.
I will use the beat-up brown pair. Grip beats looking decent.
Good. Still waiting on the replacement pair?
Yes. Between the car shop and Dr. Lenz, the Visa is at $1,428. I am knocking it down before I order.
Coffee Wednesday still good? I found a Marfa motel link that does not look like it charges Austin prices.
Send it. I am doing the $20-at-a-time method, so no fancy rooms.
You could buy a new patio chair with fewer calculations.
The old chair still holds me. Marfa would be harder to fake.
Can you still pick up the extra extension cord before Thursday, or should I add it to my gallery supply run?
I can get it if it stays under $20. My March sheet is already at $2,681 after the Cedar Bend draw and the car insurance.
Let me cover the cord from the event cash box, then. Save your room for the bigger items.
Thanks. I will still bring the mic stands and chairs early.
Reminder email is queued for 7:00. Can you check chairs and the mic before people arrive?
Yes. Phone already buzzed me for 5:15, and I copied the setup list into the little planner.
Thank you. You sounded a little thin on the call, so only do the essentials.
Essentials are enough. I took a lap around the block, made soup, and I am steadier now.
Hey, can you grab the boy from robotics Thursday at 4? Brian's stuck in the office and I'm slammed.
Yeah I can do it. Nobody to ask off from anymore, so Thursdays are mine.
Ha. Silver lining of the November shake-up I guess.
It is. Just remember the upside doesn't come with a paycheck if I take a whole day off, so don't tell him grandpa is rich.
Rough week here. The follow-up scan was clear, thank God, but the waiting wore me out.
Glad it came back clear. The waiting is the worst part. Do the next practical thing today, even a small one.
There's our line. You sound steady. Knee holding up on the Saturday walks?
Holding. Still out there every Saturday. I'd rather keep moving than sit and worry about it.
Cousin Ronnie forwarded another one of those chain emails. This time it's the 2020 ballot machines in Maricopa again. I told him I wasn't going to argue at Easter, but it wears me out.
Don't even open it. That well was poisoned a long time ago and Ronnie keeps drinking from it. The counts were certified, recounted, sued over, and certified again. There is nothing to find.
I know. It's the meanness around it that gets me, honestly. The way the bathroom-bill people and the book-banning people all show up in the same breath now.

That's exactly the part I can't stomach anymore. Daddy raised us to watch the dollars and be decent to your neighbor. I still watch the dollars. The other half of that bargain is gone from the people I used to vote for.
Walk route is flatter today. Also, the library posted the UT lecture recording you asked about.
Thanks. I will play that one later after the afternoon broadcast settles in.
Very orderly Sunday: knees first, then scholars, then whatever happens in the ninth inning.
That is about the right order. Send the link when you have a minute.
Council agenda for Thursday is up. The training and oversight item is back on, and there's a separate one about routing some welfare calls to the response team instead of patrol.
Send the link. Both of those make sense to me. Not every call needs a uniform showing up. And the training piece has been thin for years.
You'd know better than me on the call side. I only ever saw the dispatch end. But yeah, real consequences when something goes wrong is the part people skip.
I never had a stop or anything serious to draw from, just what I read and what neighbors say. The consequences part is what I keep coming back to.
Saw the flyer in the Carver Library window this morning — Mei Ann Wong and the sound piece guy on the 26th. Yours and Nora's, yes?
That's us. Different mix than last month on purpose. Reuben Diaz moved to April.
Good. Also — the Blanton's Thursday workshop on print conservation is full, but they added a 10 AM session on the 21st. I signed us up. You'll need to bring the receipt to the desk.
Thanks. Saturday walk still on for Lady Bird, 6:45 start?
How did Tuesday go? You looked tired at coffee.
Long one. Mr. Okafor's grandson tried to set him up with a password manager remotely and the recovery codes went to a Yahoo address he hasn't touched since 2011. Two hours of that.
Ha. The dispatch version of that was always 'have you tried turning it off and on again, sir.'

Also one of the regulars wanted to know if a text about her Medicare card being suspended was real. Obviously not. I am running out of nice ways to say 'if it has a countdown timer and a phone number, it is a scam.'
Did you see what Ramirez wrote under the council post about the Manor Road bike lanes? Half the old dispatch crew is in there now swinging at each other.
Saw it. Closed the tab. Not going to type into that one.
Smart. Last time you tried explaining the budget chart to that guy it read like you were picking a fight, which you weren't.
Right. Whatever I write, somebody decides I meant the worst version of it. Easier to call you Wednesday and just say it out loud.
Coffee on for Wed. Saw a kid at the counter with a UT shirt and thought of the story you told me. The summer they offered you the boards and you never went back to register for fall.
Ha. I still drive past the Tower and think about that semester I almost signed up for again.
You always say almost. Forty years of almost.
The check cleared. That settled it.
Saw the McCallum High band kids on Burnet today. Made me think of you and that story about your sister losing her flute case at the state fair in Dallas.
Ha. She still blames me. We drove back the next morning and the security guy at the fairgrounds had it behind his desk.
Only time you left the state that year, right?
Pretty much. Mom hated I-35 traffic. We barely went past Waco except for that trip.
Can we do the 22nd instead of this weekend being loose? Lucas has soccer at 10, then we can meet at Chuy's by 12:30.
The 22nd is good. Chuy's Round Rock at 12:30.
Thanks. Mom said the signature page is all she needs back, no need for a call unless something looks off.
Understood. I'll keep it simple and send it with you after lunch.
Coffee after your paperwork stop? I can meet near Hyde Park if you are staying close to 78705.
Works. I need to sign at the office first. They only need my initials and the insurance page.
You still using me as the person to call if the building can't reach you?
Yes. Emily is on the medical stuff, but the office has your number for keys and leaks.
I can come by Saturday after my appointment. Do you want me to bring anything from H-E-B?
Maybe avocados if they look decent. I've got eggs, rice, tortillas, and the last of the beans.
I will. And please do one spoonful test before you hand me the green bowl.
Noted. I may add mint to tea instead; that pot is behaving better than the basil.
Saturday route can be the flatter loop if your knee is still arguing. Are you bringing anyone to coffee after?
Flatter loop would help. No extra person this time; Sandra has her sister in town, and I need to sort Emily's packet before lunch Sunday.
Understood. I will tell the group 7:30 at the Rowing Dock lot.
Thanks. If Emily finds the missing page from Linda's stack, I may finally be done with that old folder.
The library bulletin has a Sunday porch-song pair at the Elisabet Ney courtyard. Suggested donation is $8.
That is more my speed than the arena traffic. If the knee behaves after Saturday, I may sit in the back.
Only 35 seats listed. I will forward the reservation link.
Thanks. Those close-in sets do more for me than I expect, especially when the week has been sour.
The gallery asked if you can stop by before the art talk. Their volunteer desk has three numbers on the flyer and nobody knows which one rings where.
I can come at 4:15. I'll bring the one-page log and make the greeting shorter so the volunteers don't improvise.
Thank you. Also the little desk units look newer than the ones we used last year, so I will not touch anything.
Good plan. I just need the admin screen, the ring list, and five minutes to place outside test calls.
Robotics pickup is in the gym Tuesday at 5:30. Fair warning, the line is usually on that polished floor for a while.
I can do it. I will park close and wait on the bench by the trophy case instead of standing in the line.
Thank you. And do not wear those old sneakers if you are coming straight from the trail.
New shoes only now. I learned my lesson after that granite scramble outside Fredericksburg.
After the walk, Batch has coffee and those picnic tables. They also have a new double-strength stout on the chalkboard.
Coffee first for me. If I take anything home, make it the little Mexican lager cans. I still have one beer left from the six I bought two Saturdays ago.
Noted. I will steer us to the tables by the bakery side where the air is easier.
Good plan. My lungs and my laundry both vote for that side.
Good walk this morning. Tom missed it - his neuro appointment at the VA went long Tuesday and his bursitis is flared. He says hi.
Tell him hi back. My brother-in-law swore by their ortho side for years - hope Tom gets the same luck.
Different topic - the LBJ Library has a lecture next Thursday on Republic of Texas land grants. Settler families from Tennessee and the Carolinas. Thought of you and Janet's binder.
Almost guaranteed our people are in those rolls. I'll come if the knee holds. Bring trekking poles instead of pride, as you keep telling me.
Drove past that old Stuckey building on Burnet yesterday. It's a vape shop now. Tragic.
Ha. My dad would've had words. He stood behind that counter writing up orders from 1968 until the year he retired.
Was he the guy who actually knew every part number from memory or did he just look it up like a normal human?
From memory. He'd quiz Janet and me at dinner. Mom would roll her eyes and go back to typing up the school's attendance roster at the kitchen table.
Still okay for Chuy's at 12:30? Ben wants to show you the robot arm.
Yes. I had Karen's lake loop yesterday and Rosa's old-office lunch Friday, so a quiet table sounds right.
Good. No paperwork stack today unless you ask.
Thank you. Let's just eat, catch up, and save the big forms for when they truly need eyes.
Lunch at 12:15 still okay? Mateo wants to show you the robot arm code before we leave.
Yes. I have a short Arduino tutorial queued up in case he wants to compare it.
Perfect. We should be out by 1:20 so you can get back before the opening inning.
That timing works. I will bring the enchiladas and leave the small radio in the truck.
The grandson's counselor sent a form asking parents' education levels. What do I put for grandpa, just for the family tree section?
Aunt Janet asked if you saw the photos I put up from the robotics meet. She said she can't find them.

Two years at UT, no diploma. Put it however the form lets you.
There's a 'some college' bubble. That works. He asked once why you have all those phone-company patches and no graduation photo. I told him you went to work instead.
Will do. Also Nora tagged you in some gallery thing on the other app this morning — you never react over there, I had to text you to make sure you saw it.
That's the short version, and it's true.
Saw it, saved it. I just read on that one. Easier than trying to keep up with all the little buttons.

Dad question. Aiden's robotics teacher sent home a flyer about a 'health freedom' speaker at the library Thursday. The flyer is doing rounds in the parent group chat. Some moms are forwarding it as if it's real news.
Is the speaker the one with the YouTube channel about 5G and the hospitals.
Kai asked at lunch why Grandpa went to the thing on the lawn earlier this month. I told him what I knew but figured you'd want to answer it.
That's the guy.
Tell him I wanted to stand with neighbors and put a little money toward people who needed lawyers. I went once, by daylight, listened more than I talked.
He also asked if you'd ever been picked up by police. I said no, but you tell him.
Never have. Closest was a taillight stop in '08 and a warning. That's the whole record. I'll tell him Sunday.

Same circuit I keep cleaning up after at the center. He recycles the same three claims that got Mrs. Delgado convinced last spring that her cardiologist was lying to her. I will not be polite about that one. Tell the parent group to look at who is paying for the venue before they forward it again.
Logan's history class is doing a 'where your family is from' poster. He asked me to fill in Grandpa's row.
Tell him the easy version. Born in Waco, grew up in Austin from grade school on, never really left except work trips.
He wants the hospital too if you remember it. You know how he is.
Hillcrest Baptist. Mom said it was a thunderstorm afternoon. Janet would know better than me, ask her Sunday.
I found the old family photos. Also, did you ever schedule the work Dr. Lenz mentioned last fall?
Not yet. I waited after the first estimate jumped. The March check was only a look and a receipt request.
Do the next practical thing. Pay what you can and keep the appointment notes together.
That is the plan. Another $95 goes to Visa Friday, then I will see where the shoes and the follow-up fit.
Saw your letter to the editor in the Statesman about the Cap Metro extension. Solid. You sound like one of those old yellow-dog guys but with a calculator.
Ha. I'll take it. I just want the route built and the bonds priced honestly. Houston paid too much for theirs and they're still arguing about it.
You ever miss when the other side at least talked roads and budgets instead of which books the library can shelve?
Every day. That's not where I live anymore. Hasn't been since they started cheering people who wouldn't accept a count they lost.
Quick panic — Marisol's bio for the April talk never came in. Can you cover the intro if she doesn't send by Friday?
Yes. I'll write a short one from her gallery page tonight and have it ready Friday morning. If I told you I'd handle setup, I'll handle this too.
You are the calmest person in my phone. Thank you.
Curious to hear her talk, honestly. I'll be there at 5:30 to set chairs and the mic, same as last month.

Mei Ann confirmed she'll bring two pieces. Also Reuben asked if April could be a joint slot with Awa Camara — she does West African textile work, just moved to Austin. I said yes if you're good with it.
Good with it. That's exactly the kind of pairing the talks should be doing. Add her.
One more — the Blanton's spring members lecture is the 28th, Carmen Herrera retrospective. I have an extra ticket if you want it.
Yes please. I'll meet you there 6:00 — and bring the April flyer draft so we can mark it up after.
Can you cover robotics pickup this afternoon, or is this one of your paddle days?
I can get him if you need me. My court slot is 3:30, but I can skip the last game and still get the side-step practice in.
Only if it does not mess up Saturday. You were annoyed enough missing that icy morning last month.
Saturday is safe. Karen is talking Hill Country only if someone drives; otherwise we do the water-side loop.
Did the sink repair turn out as badly as the first man guessed? I worried about that all afternoon.
How is the budget feeling this month? You mentioned the premium hike was rough.
It came to $386. I paid it and moved the receipt into the March folder. I will feel that one for a bit.
Tighter. The marketplace plan jumped again and I'm covering the whole thing myself now. Two clients only this quarter, so the math is closer than I'd like.
Do the next practical thing. Have you thought about picking up a third contract, or is that against the whole reason you stepped back in November?
I am glad you could handle it. Do the next practical thing.
That's the tension. The whole point of cutting back was the knee, the studio time, and Sundays with Emily and the boy. Adding a third would undo it. I'll trim spending instead.
That is the plan. Sunday I will tighten groceries and leave the car alone unless the light comes back on.
Davis sang 'In the Garden' at school chapel today. He kept asking me what 'tarry' meant. Made me laugh.
That's the one Mama used to hum at the sink. Tell him I'll show him the verse on Sunday and what Grandma's hymnal looks like.
He'd love that. Speaking of - Sunday the 29th, are you coming to the early service with us or just meeting at Cracker Barrel on 183 after? Need to RSVP for brunch either way.
Service. Haven't been inside in months and Davis singing 'In the Garden' has me feeling it. I'll bring the hymnal.
Dad, if you want, I can print the Mayo page from work before Sunday lunch.
That would help. The county notice was clear, but I like having one more plain explanation before I schedule the next one.
I will bring it with the insurance folder. Please ignore Uncle Ray's group text until then.
Already did. All caps and no source is not my favorite combination.
Do you want me to print those Bexar forms at work, or are you still waiting?
Please wait. I am only cleaning up the folder for the first Thursday table right now.
Got it. After the car and dentist stuff, skipping the hotel weekend makes sense.
Yes. I will keep the papers sorted and pick a quieter set of dates.
Heads up — Jordan's robotics club fees are due next week. $85. Will that hit you wrong this month?
No, I'm covered. Wagner came in at $1,830 for March, better than I projected on Tuesday.
That's a step up from Feb. Good month?
Held at 26 hrs most weeks. With the SS deposit that puts March right around $4,130 before taxes. I'll Venmo you the $85 tonight.
Caleb asked if he could crash at your place after robotics night Friday.
He can come over for pizza, but sleeping there is awkward. The couch is short and the bedroom is all I have.
Fair. We'll pick him up by 9:30. Did the office finally handle that renewal form?
Turned in today. Same unit, another year, and they fixed the latch without charging me.
The HOA wants me to vote on the landscaping contract by Friday. I have no idea what to do with two unknown names.
See if your HOA put out a side-by-side, or ask both to write a short statement. That's how the booklet I use does it and it makes a real difference.
You really do read those things every time, don't you.
Every time. Even the school board races. If I'm asked to pick somebody, I want to know they can actually run the thing once they're in.
Found the picture from Mom's retirement at Pflugerville Elementary. The principal gave her that wooden apple plaque, 23 years in the front office.
I remember. The teachers all signed the back of it. She kept it on the bookcase next to Dad's parts catalog binder.
Speaking of, I scanned his Stuckey 25-year pin certificate too. Want me to bring both to lunch Sunday so you can pick what to keep?
I found Aunt Celia's Santa Fe envelope in the blue folder. Do you want copies before I put it back?
Yes, please. That may be my excuse to go back when the room rates behave.
Then do the next practical thing: copy first, room later.
Already moved $15 this morning. No bookstore order this month.
Saturday route — south shore again? Or the Pflugerville trail. I have a flyer for the Bullock Museum talk on McLennan County in the 50s, thought you might want it.
South shore is fine for the knee. McLennan, ha. That's home turf for the first few years of mine. I'll take the flyer.
Figured. Did your family come up to Austin when you were small or were you older?
Small. Grade school. Same house off Manchaca until I left for work. Janet and I both finished at Travis.
FYI the Saturday hiking page had a small back-and-forth overnight about whether to move the start to 7. Someone got snippy. Don't wade in if you haven't yet.
I scrolled it at breakfast and put the phone down. Going to bring it up in person at the trailhead instead.
Good. Tone reads wrong in those threads. I read your comment last month three different ways before I realized you were agreeing with me.
Exactly the reason. I'll just say it Saturday.
Coffee Wednesday is still on my calendar. Same place unless the students invade every table again.
Same place. I put it in the phone and the paper book, because apparently one reminder is only a suggestion.
You bringing that novel Karen mentioned, or the famous bill spreadsheet?
Novel. The sheet can wait. I had two gray mornings this week, so I am choosing coffee and a walk before numbers.
Rangers at 7. You still doing coffee tomorrow, or did Rao change your pills again?
Coffee is fine. Same two generics, just take one after dinner now. Cheaper that way if I stay with the 90-day fill.
That is the most retired sentence you have ever typed.
Maybe. I still need to skip the ballpark nachos if I want decent numbers Monday morning.
Heads up - the landlord on the East Cesar Chavez space bumped our April rent by 22%. If we lose that room, the talks will have to move to the library annex or pause.
That's brutal. That whole strip is being priced for tech offices. We are losing the rooms where regular Austin actually meets.
I know. Can you draft something for the council's cultural preservation overlay hearing on the 31st? Yours always lands better than mine.

Can you check the gallery chairs tomorrow after your usual loop? I can meet at 8:15 with the flyer proofs.
Yes. I am doing the trail first, probably 6:30 from the Lamar side, then I will come by.
Perfect. The forecast looks rude after midmorning, so that timing is smart.
It is the part of the day that still feels unclaimed. I will bring the spare extension cord too.

Put one Shiner or Dos Equis in for me. Leave the big bottle for Daniel. That will make three beers for me since last Sunday.

Thank you. Easier on my throat, and I can hear the robotics stories better from there.
The lecture ticket is $18 if we register today. Should I hold one for you?

Done. You can hand me cash Saturday after the walk.
